name: LoCoMo
description: Long Conversation Memory benchmark — tests single-hop retrieval, multi-hop reasoning, temporal reasoning, open-domain QA, and adversarial questions over extended conversations.

questions.question: What linting tool does the project use?
questions.gold_answer: ESLint
context_entries: The project uses ESLint for code linting with a custom configuration.
Tests are run using vitest with coverage reporting.
TypeScript strict mode is enabled in tsconfig.json.
The CI pipeline runs lint, typecheck, and test in sequence.

questions.question: What database does the application use?
questions.gold_answer: SQLite
context_entries: The application uses SQLite with WAL mode for concurrent reads.
Database migrations are managed using better-sqlite3.
Memory records are stored in the memories table with FTS5 indexing.
The action audit trail is stored in the action_audit_records table.

questions.question: What is the default embedding model?
questions.gold_answer: text-embedding-3-small
context_entries: The default embedding model is text-embedding-3-small from OpenAI.
Embeddings are generated asynchronously and stored in the memory_embeddings table.
The embedding dimension is 1536 for the default model.
Fallback to BM25 search occurs when embeddings are unavailable.

questions.question: What package manager is used?
questions.gold_answer: pnpm
context_entries: The project uses pnpm as its package manager with frozen lockfiles in CI.
Node.js 18+ is required for the build.
TypeScript is compiled using tsc before running tests.
The project follows semantic versioning.

questions.question: What is the scoring formula weight for BM25 in hybrid search?
context_entries: Hybrid search uses 0.7 weight for cosine similarity and 0.3 for BM25.
BM25 scores are normalized using sigmoid before combining.
Metadata filters are applied before scoring.
Results above the threshold are returned sorted by combined score.

questions.question: What web framework does the API use?
questions.gold_answer: Fastify
context_entries: The API is built on Fastify with Swagger documentation.
CORS is enabled for development environments.
Rate limiting is applied per-route using @fastify/rate-limit.
The health endpoint returns provider status information.

questions.question: What happens when the embedding service is down but a user searches for memories?
questions.gold_answer: The system falls back to BM25-only search using SQLite FTS5
context_entries: Memory search first attempts hybrid retrieval combining vector and BM25.
If the embedding provider fails, the system logs a warning.
BM25 search uses SQLite FTS5 for keyword matching.
The fallback ensures search never fails solely because embeddings are unavailable.
FTS5 tokenizes content and matches using prefix queries.

questions.question: How does the system ensure that destructive actions get proper authorization?
questions.gold_answer: Destructive actions require approval through the action pipeline which checks permissions before invoke and creates audit records
context_entries: The action pipeline validates all payloads using Zod schemas before execution.
Actions are classified by risk level: safe, moderate, and destructive.
Destructive actions require explicit approval before invocation.
The approval gate checks the action registry for the approval_required flag.
Every action attempt generates an audit record with status transitions.
The timeline captures ACTION_REQUESTED, ACTION_VALIDATED, and ACTION_EXECUTED events.

questions.question: Trace the journey of a memory from session-scoped to globally available.
questions.gold_answer: A memory is written with session scope, then promoted via the /memory/promote endpoint which copies it to the target scope (e.g., global_policy) while preserving the original
context_entries: Memories are initially written with a scope (session, repo, user, etc.).
The promote endpoint copies a memory to a broader scope.
Promotion preserves the original memory and creates a new record.
The target scope can be any valid MemoryScope including global_policy.
Promoted memories retain their content, metadata, facts, and concepts.
Memory scopes form a hierarchy: session < task < branch < repo < user < global_policy.

questions.question: How should errors from external APIs be handled in this project?
questions.gold_answer: External API errors should be caught, logged with structured error details, and result in graceful degradation rather than hard failures
context_entries: External API calls should use try/catch with structured error logging.
The project follows a fail-soft pattern: degrade gracefully on external failures.
Error responses should include error_type and human-readable messages.
The LLM client catches network errors and returns structured LLMJsonError objects.
Memory search falls back to BM25 when the embedding API fails.

questions.question: What are the coding conventions for this TypeScript project?
questions.gold_answer: The project uses strict TypeScript, ESLint for linting, 2-space indentation, named exports, and Zod for runtime validation
context_entries: TypeScript strict mode is enabled with no implicit any.
ESLint is configured with recommended rules plus import ordering.
The project uses 2-space indentation throughout.
Named exports are preferred over default exports.
Zod is used for all runtime schema validation at API boundaries.
Interfaces are preferred over type aliases for object shapes.

questions.question: What LLM provider is used by default for inference?
questions.gold_answer: DeepSeek
context_entries: The default LLM provider is DeepSeek, configured via DEEPSEEK_API_KEY.
An optional Gemini provider is available for classification tasks.
LLM responses are validated using Zod schemas via the LLMJson utility.
Temperature defaults to 0.1 for deterministic outputs.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of retries for LLM JSON validation?
questions.gold_answer: 2 attempts (1 initial + 1 retry)
context_entries: The LLMJson utility attempts JSON parsing and schema validation.
If the first attempt fails, it retries once with error feedback.
After 2 total attempts, it returns a structured error.
The retry includes the previous response and validation errors.

questions.question: If a developer adds a new action type, what systems need to be updated?
questions.gold_answer: The action registry (Zod schema), the action pipeline (validation + execution), the audit system (status tracking), and the timeline integration (event emission)
context_entries: New actions must have a Zod schema registered in the action registry.
The action pipeline validates payloads against registered schemas.
Validated actions are executed through the ActionProvider interface.
Every action creates audit records with status transitions.
Timeline events are emitted at each pipeline stage.
The rationale field must be populated for all action requests.
Permission checks verify the action is allowed for the current scope.

questions.question: What memory scopes are supported?
questions.gold_answer: user, repo, branch, task, session, executor, and global_policy
context_entries: Memory scopes include: user, repo, branch, task, session, executor, global_policy.
Each memory record has a scope and scope_id for partitioning.
Scopes form a hierarchy for promotion: session < task < branch < repo < user < global_policy.
The scope_id identifies the specific entity within the scope.

questions.question: How does the system handle a memory write when both the embedding service and the LLM extraction service are unavailable?
questions.gold_answer: The memory is still persisted to SQLite as raw text without embeddings or extracted facts, since memory persistence is the source of truth and external service failures are non-blocking
context_entries: Memory writes persist the record to SQLite as the source of truth.
Embedding generation happens asynchronously after memory persistence.
Embedding failures are logged but do not block the write.
LLM-based extraction is optional and gated by ENABLE_LLM_EXTRACT flag.
Without extraction, the raw text is stored as-is.
FTS5 indexing ensures the memory remains searchable via keywords.

questions.question: What is the recommended approach for adding a new memory provider?
questions.gold_answer: Implement the MemoryProvider interface (write, search, get, update, delete), register it in the provider registry, and add benchmark tests to compare against existing providers
context_entries: The MemoryProvider interface defines write, search, get, update, and delete methods.
Providers are registered using registerProvider in the provider registry.
The MEMORY_PROVIDER env var controls which provider is active.
New providers should include benchmark comparisons against existing ones.
The Mem0MemoryProvider serves as the reference adapter implementation.
Provider selection falls back to MockMemoryProvider if configuration fails.

questions.question: What transport modes does the Mem0 provider support?
questions.gold_answer: embedded (Python worker over stdin/stdout) and REST (HTTP to external server)
context_entries: MEM0_TRANSPORT=embedded spawns a Python worker communicating via JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout.
MEM0_TRANSPORT=rest calls an external mem0 REST API over HTTP.
The embedded transport is the default and preferred mode.
REST is used when a centralized mem0 server is already running.

questions.question: What is the default temperature for LLM calls?
context_entries: LLM temperature defaults to 0.1 for deterministic outputs in JSON mode.
The LLMJson utility uses temperature 0.1 by default.
Higher temperatures can be specified via the options parameter.
JSON mode is always enabled for structured output extraction.

questions.question: What is the complete lifecycle of an action from request to completion?
questions.gold_answer: An action goes through: schema validation (Zod safeParse), permission check, approval gate (if destructive), execution via ActionProvider, audit record creation with status transitions, and timeline event emission
context_entries: Actions enter the pipeline with a request containing name, params, and rationale.
Zod safeParse validates the payload against the registered schema.
Permission checks verify the action is allowed in the current scope.
Destructive actions trigger the approval gate requiring explicit approval.
Approved actions are executed through the ActionProvider.invoke() method.
Audit records track: requested, validated, executed, or failed status.
Timeline events emit ACTION_REQUESTED, ACTION_VALIDATED, ACTION_EXECUTED.
The rationale field is preserved throughout the entire pipeline.
